content.value_statement: Frontend layouts often break across mobile, tablet, and desktop screens. This skill guides responsive React, Tailwind, and CSS implementation with mobile-first patterns.
actual_capabilities: Guide React component layout updates for .tsx and .jsx files.
Apply Tailwind responsive utilities across standard breakpoints.
Plan CSS Grid and Flexbox layouts for changing viewport sizes.
Improve navigation, typography, spacing, and tap targets for smaller screens.
Check responsive behavior across mobile, tablet, and desktop breakpoints.
limitations: Does not include the external responsive standards file referenced by the skill.
Does not run browser tests by itself.
Does not provide visual assets or design system tokens.
Depends on the host project for framework and CSS configuration.

use_cases.title: Adapt React Screens
use_cases.description: Make existing React screens adapt cleanly across viewport sizes.

use_cases.title: Standardize Components
use_cases.description: Review components for consistent breakpoints, spacing, typography, and touch targets.

use_cases.title: Plan Responsive Checks
use_cases.description: Create responsive test scenarios for mobile, tablet, and desktop layouts.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Component Responsive
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React component and update the layout for mobile, tablet, and desktop screens. Keep the existing design intent.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Fixed Spacing
prompt_templates.prompt: Replace fixed pixel-heavy layout choices with relative units and responsive spacing. Explain the main layout changes.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Navigation Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt this navigation menu for small screens with touch-friendly controls, clear breakpoints, and accessible interaction states.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Full Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this page for responsive risks across React structure, Tailwind classes, typography, media assets, and breakpoint behavior. Prioritize fixes by impact.

output_examples.input: A React dashboard uses fixed columns and cramped mobile controls.
output_examples.output: The response identifies fixed width panels, proposes a stacked mobile layout, adjusts breakpoints, and recommends larger touch targets.

output_examples.input: A Tailwind navigation bar does not fit small screens.
output_examples.output: The response recommends a compact mobile menu, breakpoint-specific spacing, clearer wrapping rules, and keyboard-accessible controls.

output_examples.input: A product page uses large images and fixed typography.
output_examples.output: The response suggests responsive image sizing, fluid type scales, and testing steps for mobile, tablet, and desktop screens.

best_practices: Start with mobile layout before adding tablet and desktop breakpoints.
Use relative units and fluid containers when fixed pixels would break layouts.
Test key workflows at mobile, tablet, and desktop widths.
anti_patterns: Adding desktop-only styles before defining a usable mobile layout.
Using fixed widths that force horizontal scrolling on small screens.
Reducing visual size without checking tap targets and readable typography.

faq.question: Does this skill write React components?
faq.answer: It can guide React component edits when the user asks for responsive layout work.

faq.question: Can it help with Tailwind CSS?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers responsive Tailwind utilities, including common breakpoint prefixes.

faq.question: Does it include browser automation?
faq.answer: No. It suggests responsive checks, but testing tools depend on the host project.

faq.question: Can it improve mobile navigation?
faq.answer: Yes. It gives guidance for menus, touch targets, and layout changes across screen sizes.

faq.question: Is it limited to React?
faq.answer: React is mentioned directly, but the CSS guidance also applies to many frontend stacks.

faq.question: Does it rely on external files?
faq.answer: The skill references a relative standards file outside its package, which should be bundled or removed.
